edges.description: Shows that loss of ANO3 can make neurons hyperexcitable, which is the kind of change the node proposes, but in a different neuron type and through a different potassium channel.
edges.limitations: The neurons are peripheral nociceptors, not striatal medium spiny neurons. The potassium current affected is the sodium-activated Slack current, which the dystonia-variant cell study found unaffected; that study implicates KCa3.1 instead. The model is a complete knockout, whereas patients carry one heterozygous, mostly missense, allele whose direction of effect is unresolved. No dystonia or other motor phenotype was reported.

nodes.description: ANO3 is a calcium-activated phospholipid scramblase of the TMEM16 family, present largely in intracellular membranes. One group reports that it also conducts ions; another, studying human TMEM16C isoforms, found scrambling but no ion transport. How disease variants change scrambling itself has not been measured directly in the cited studies; what has been measured is their effect on cellular calcium signalling, recorded in the next node.

nodes.description: Heterozygous ANO3 variants, almost all missense, spread across the protein rather than clustered in one domain. The two original familial variants lie in exon 15; many later childhood-onset variants are de novo, and one review proposes that variants near the scrambling domain track the more severe early-onset phenotype. The functional impact category is left unset on purpose: whether pathogenic variants reduce or alter ANO3 function is disputed (see the knowledge-gap discussion). The ANO3 gene binding sits on the next node, with the molecular function it encodes.

nodes.description: Cells expressing ANO3 variants show compromised activation of the calcium-dependent potassium channel KCa3.1. In rat sensory neurons ANO3 instead supports the sodium-activated potassium channel Slack (KCNT1), and its loss there raises excitability; in the dystonia-variant study the sodium-activated channels were not affected, so which potassium current matters in the striatum is not established.

nodes.description: The inferred cellular substrate of the movement disorder. A PubMed search for ANO3 with mouse, mice or knockout returned no animal model of dystonia. The step from this node to dystonic movement is likewise inferred, and the edges to the movement phenotypes below are uncited for that reason.

nodes.description: A knockout rat studied for pain processing, not for movement. In dorsal root ganglion nociceptors, loss of TMEM16C reduced expression of the sodium-activated potassium channel Slack, broadened action potentials and raised excitability, and the animals were more sensitive to heat and mechanical stimuli. No motor or dystonic phenotype is reported, and the striatum was not examined.
